spec.name: News tone v13
spec.notes: Long names with improving news sentiment.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.1, annual return 3%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.07 to 1.16 (change +0.09).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.07 to 1.07. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 0.90 (as submitted, 3 bps: 1.07); it breaks even at 47.6 bps with daily turnover 0.03.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.07 against 1.07 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -0.12 against 1.07 in research, a gap of +1.19.
The best year gives 50% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 54%; Sharpe is 0.86 in calm and 1.67 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 257 distinct specs; the best of 257 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 1.13, so the claimed 1.10 becomes -0.03 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 48%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.14 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.00, 95th percentile 0.80).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.07 to as low as 0.12 (as low as 0.55 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (11 days) give 58% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 42% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
